To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lipid signatures are highly dynamic during early adult life but remarkably stable during aging.

(i) the lipidome composition of Drosophila flies is highly dynamic during early adulthood and is characterized by a rapid and pronounced increase in storage lipid content, (ii) the lipidome is remarkably stable during adult life and (iii) the lipidome of genetically obese flies is altered during early adulthood, while it is almost unaltered in comparison to normal flies during adult life.
the storage lipid triacylglycerol is the most abundant and most diverse lipid class in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, which is used for both, membrane formation and as an energy reserve.

the identification of the mechanisms that control the accumulation and mobilization of storage lipid in insects and their impact on lifespan and aging.
the identification of lipid species that are involved in the regulation of lifespan in insects.

a fundamental understanding of the molecular mechanisms of aging and lifespan determination in insects and provides a novel platform for the identification of novel targets for anti-aging interventions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lipidome is remarkably stable throughout aging, but that a characteristic lipid signature is associated with moribund flies.
we have established a single-fly mass-spectrometry-based lipidomic approach and used this approach to study the aging and lipid homeostasis in Drosophila.
lipid signatures of normal and obese flies are largely stable throughout life, except for a rapid and selective TAG depletion close to death.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the lipidome is remarkably stable during adult and senesce life, and that the lipid signature of morbid flies is distinct from healthy and aging flies, which is of relevance in the context of the aging process and the onset of diseases.
we provide the first comprehensive lipidome analysis of normal and obese aging flies, which reveals that storage lipid accumulation is a life-limiting process.
